title: Monthly roadmap alignment packet — decision accelerators & signal atlas
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Provide a compact, decision-oriented packet for the monthly exec alignment meeting focused on inference roadmap priorities, trade-offs, and immediate asks. This document is designed to accelerate decisions by surface-leveling: 1) the minimal set of outstanding decisions required this cycle; 2) signal definitions & thresholds for OKR progress; 3) short remediation/playbook lanes for regressions or capacity shortfalls.

Scope: Covers product and platform asks across Hosted API, Dedicated, and Private deployments where roadmap choices materially affect unit economics, SLO exposure, and go-to-market timing. Not a full program brief — this is an executive decision accelerator.

Core sections:
- Executive summary (1 page): should contain the single ask, why now, and upside/downside scenarios.
- Decision table: explicit options (A/B/C), owners, trade-offs, and recommended path.
- Signal Atlas: concrete metrics, measurement queries, alert thresholds, owner, and short-term mitigations. Examples: tokens-per-request median, 95th latency tail per region, dedicated pool utilization, eval regression count on golden prompt set.
- OKR delta view: which initiatives move the needle (cost/latency/reliability), current status versus target, and next actions to keep or change course.
- Risk lanes & contingency plans: capacity shortage playbook, model-quality rollback steps, and customer-communication template.
- Asks & commit table: funding, headcount, infra swaps, or runway changes with a required decision date.

Intended outcome for the meeting: a clear decision or an explicit go/no-go with a timeboxed follow-up and action owners. If an ask is deferred, state the minimal telemetry and gating criteria required to reconsider.

Why this is different: rather than summarizing every project, this packet prioritizes decisions that change roadmap shape or budget allocation in the next 60 days and supplies concrete, actionable signals (Signal Atlas) rather than only progress narratives.

Notes on signal examples (not exhaustive):
- Token unit economics: monthly rolling cost-per-1k-tokens for top-10 customers, owner: Pricing (Miguel Ramos), threshold: >7% week-over-week increase triggers review.
- Latency SLO: p95 < 250ms global for small-gen routes, owner: Infra (Leah Gupta), threshold: breach for 3 consecutive 1-hour windows triggers automatic canary rollback.
- Dedicated pool CPU/GPU contention: sustained utilization >85% for 30m triggers burst provisioning policy, owner: Dedicated PM (Marco Chen).
- Eval signal: golden-pairs failing >2% vs baseline in last 48h, owner: Applied ML (Riley Thompson), threshold triggers revert or focused calibration.

Operational checklist (pre-meeting):
1) Engineering to attach dashboards + 30-day trend snapshots.
2) Applied ML to provide top-5 prompt regressions and repro steps.
3) Finance to validate cost delta scenarios for proposed infra changes.
4) PM to prepare one-slide decision table and recommended path.

Post-meeting cadence: action owners commit to explicit deliverables (owner/date), status updates flow into the fortnightly Ops sync. Non-decision items get moved to the backlog with a re-evaluation gating condition defined in the packet.
